errors.statement: In the combined day and evening bill part, the chance rises more with day charge for customers without voice-mail messages: about 2% to 11%, against about 1% to 2% with messages (and a plan).
errors.check: probe --hold typical, day charge 19.07 -> 42.40 at (plan 0, 0 messages) and (plan 1, 17 messages): ann_89 goes -0.552 -> -0.316 and -0.071 -> +0.165, the same +0.236 both times, so the part carries no message interaction (C116 did-through-part -0.077). The stated 2.26% -> 10.55% vs 1.46% -> 1.78% are the whole-model group numbers (identical to C103, the voice-mail-plan gate in ann_88). The interaction is put in the wrong part, but the numbers hold for the whole model, and the paragraph gives whole-model risks throughout (as in the C115 sentence). Under K3, a whole-model effect stated as a part's effect that reproduces at whole-model scope is weakened, not refuted.

errors.statement: A higher daytime charge lowers it steadily up to about 15.64 US dollars (between 7.93 and 31.04 for different customers), then no further; about 11% at 19.07 to about 2% at 42.40; flattening because the chance cannot go much lower.
errors.check: probe --hold typical, 3 calls, Idaho, day charge 10/15.64/19.07/25/31/34/42.4 --wide: ann_90 +2.94, +2.17, +1.70, +0.90, +0.08, +0.07, +0.07; risk 11.3% at 19.07, 2.4% at 31. The typical case flattens at about 31.5 (hinge 5395 switching off, not saturation), right at the top of the stated 7.93-31.04 spread. 15.64 is the median fold across customers. Direction, spread and risk numbers hold; the 'then no further' point is wrong for the sentence's own example. Weakened (median threshold given with 'about' and a spread).

errors.statement: In the combined bill part more voice-mail messages raise the chance, while across the whole model they lower it.
errors.check: probe --hold typical, plan = 1, messages 0/17/36: whole-model risk 0.3%, 0.9%, 1.8% (rising). C025 (linked.moved: plan switched on with the first message) has mean log-odds -2.47 at 0 and -3.89 at 17, rising after that: the whole-model lowering is the plan switching on. Under the claim's linked reading (customers with messages, who all have a plan, against those without) the lowering holds for real people, so not refuted. The message effect itself raises risk for plan holders.

errors.statement: Daytime minutes add to it in stages above about 204 minutes: for a typical customer without a plan, 0 to 271 minutes moves it from about 2% to about 21%.
errors.check: C107 is a part-scope claim for highDayUsageHinges (ann_88). Both verifiers' rechecks reproduce it (threshold 203.6 for all 2939 non-plan customers). In the block for the whole usageAndServiceRisk part, 2% -> 21% reads as whole-model, where verifier A's probe gives 16.3% at 0 minutes and 50.0% at 271 (ann_90 on for light users, the cascade adding). The numbers reproduce at the part's own scope: weakened.

errors.statement: In the near-constant chain, more voice-mail messages raise the chance steadily, from about 2% to about 2%; a small nudge that barely moves.
errors.check: C144 reproduces (+0.079 log-odds, 2.26% -> 2.44%). probe --hold typical over service calls 1/4/7: ann_96 -0.028, +0.014, +0.181, larger than the message effect (-0.028 -> +0.060 over 0-36 messages with a plan). The text presents messages as the chain's driver, and '2% to 2%' says nothing. True as stated but not exhaustive: weakened.

errors.statement: A higher daytime charge holds it back, more for light daytime users.
errors.check: Day-charge sweep at 3 calls (E2): the brake acts only while the charge is below about 31.5 US dollars, so it acts in the light-use range, and light users with many calls get the higher risk. 'Holds it back, more for light users' has a reading under which it holds (the charge's damping works in the light-use range), but it is garbled as written. The service-call half reproduces. Weakened.

errors.statement: Higher daytime minutes raise it, even more so with at most one call: about 2% to 9% with at most one call, and about 6% to 9% with more calls.
errors.check: probe --hold typical, 126 min / 21.42 vs 236 min / 40.12 US dollars: 1 call 2.3% -> 7.1%, 2 calls 2.9% -> 7.1% (rises), 4 calls 35.9% -> 14.9% (falls; ann_90 +3.15 -> +0.78). C059's group mean through the part for more than 1 call is -0.26. The rise holds for the typical member of the group (2 calls) but not for the group as a whole: weakened.

errors.statement: Title 'Service calls for light daytime users'.
errors.check: Same probe as E7: at 236 minutes and 4 calls ann_90 still adds +0.78 (hinge 9203, which does not read day use). The title is a simplification that fits only hinge 5395: weakened.
